notes: §1985:VI.6.5.4 GR9: "TIME is composed of the data elements hours, minutes, seconds, and hundredths of a second" on a 24-hour clock, it "behaves as if it had been described in a COBOL program as an unsigned elementary numeric integer data item eight digits in length", and "The minimum value of TIME is 00000000; the maximum value of TIME is 23595999". AcceptSource.Time reads the run unit's clock once and returns hour * 1000000 + minute * 10000 + second * 100 + millisecond / 10: the .NET reading has hours 0 to 23, minutes and seconds 0 to 59 and milliseconds 0 to 999, so the value lies in 00000000 to 23595999 and the hundredths are real (the zero-fill sentence is for a system without them). BindAccept binds FROM TIME for every edition as a conceptual unsigned PIC 9(8) DISPLAY item (ConceptualItem, ConceptualDigits) and an implicit MOVE from it to identifier-2, and EmitAcceptTemporal fills the item from the clock and emits that MOVE, so the eight-digit integer reaches each receiver by the MOVE rules (§1985:VI.6.5.4 GR6). The 2023 difference, a seconds value above 59 under >>LEAP-SECOND ON, is unreachable at 85: the directive is refused (COBOL0900) and the clock reading never carries second 60. Probed at --std 85 with the clock pinned (WISEOWL_COBOL_CLOCK): 14:41:00 gives 14410000, 23:59:59.999 gives 23595999, 00:00:00 gives 00000000, 09:05:07.129 gives 09050712; the same reading stores as 0014410000 in 9(10), 410000 in 9(6), +14410000.00 in S9(8)V99, 14410000 in 9(8) COMP, left-justified and space-filled in X(10) and a group, 1441 in X(4), right-justified in a JUSTIFIED item and 14 41 00 00 in 99B99B99B99. The witness accepts TIME into a 9(8) item (numeric, at most 23595999, each part in range) and into an X(10) item (eight digits and two spaces).

next.reason: 1985: 'The minimum value of TIME is 00000000; the maximum value of TIME is 23595999.' §2023:14.9.1.4 GR11 keeps the 8-digit hhmmsscc layout, the 24-hour basis and zero for unavailable fractions, but makes the seconds range '00 through 59 when a LEAP-SECOND directive with the OFF phrase is in effect' or '00 through nn, where nn is defined by the implementor, when a LEAP-SECOND directive with the ON phrase is in effect'; under ON 'the implementor defines whether a value greater than 59 may be reported' (§2023:7.3.17.4 GR2). The implied OFF default (§2023:7.3.17.4 GR1, GR3) keeps 1985 programs at 23595999, but a program 2023 accepts (with >>LEAP-SECOND ON) gets an implementor-defined maximum: a case added, the fixed maximum made implementor-defined.
